title: Optimize walkthrough — cost modeling, batching & KV-prefix cache with Aurum Financial
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Aurum Financial through Optimize recommendations for batching and prefix/KV cache, ran a live cost-model simulation for their low-latency customer support scoring workload, discussed hosted vs dedicated latency tradeoffs, and agreed on next steps to run a 2-week POC with a tailored cost spreadsheet and sample traces.
topics: Cost model assumptions and per-token economics
SLOs and deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)
next_steps: Jordan Diaz: Send tailored cost-model spreadsheet and console demo recording (due: 2027-03-04)
Priya Nair: Prepare sample inference traces + ideal prefix keys for KV cache (due: 2027-03-05)
Schedule POC kickoff (customer + Redwood infra) for week of 2027-03-15
action_items: Jordan Diaz: Share customized cost model CSV and assumptions (due: 2027-03-04)
Priya Nair: Run quick throughput sim with Aurum sample traces and share result sheet (due: 2027-03-05)
Marta Ruiz: Provide 48h of anonymized session traces and latency percentiles (due: 2027-03-05)
transcript:
Header: 2027-03-02 16:00 UTC — Duration 42m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Aurum ML), Ethan (Infra), Ravi (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick demo of Redwood Optimize + console, focused on batching and prefix/KV caching. Live cost model simulation for a chat-based scoring pipeline.

[00:00] Jordan: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can see names, cool, i'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our SE, we'll do a 30-ish minute walkthrough of Optimize recommendations and then run a small cost simulation against the traces Marta shared.
[00:18] Marta: hey Jordan, thanks, excited, we mostly want to see how much we can shave off token costs without breaking our 95th pct latency SLAs — we target sub 120ms p95 for scoring.
[00:31] Priya: great, that's helpful — can you confirm average prompt length and reply length? you mentioned short prompts, longer responses?
[00:39] Marta: yeah average prompt is like 45 tokens, output is around 120 tokens for the scoring call. sessions are sticky — users can re-query context, so there's a session id each user.
[00:51] Ethan: and infra note — we are on GCP with a VPC, want to know if private deployment is required for certs, but initially host is ok for proof.
[01:02] Jordan: perfect. high-level, Optimize has two levers — batching/concurrency and prefix (session) or KV caching. for your pattern, prefix cache any repeated context per session tends to give big token savings since the model doesn't recompute the history.
[01:18] Marta: when you say prefix cache, is that the same as the session KV cache we saw in docs?
[01:23] Priya: similar. prefix cache keeps decoded KV for recent prefixes, KV-store approach lets you look up larger context windows. there's a tradeoff: prefix is low latency, small memory; KV allows partial lookups for large histories but can add lookup cost.
[01:37] Ravi: can you quantify the lookup overhead? network hop vs token savings?
[01:42] Priya: good question — in our sim we model a KV lookup as ~3-6ms extra on average when it's remote, but it prevents sending the full prefix which could be dozens to hundreds of tokens saved — so net is often positive. if you colocate KV near GPUs or use in-memory prefix cache on node, the lookup is <1ms.
[02:01] Jordan: i'll share the sheet shortly, but high level for Aurum's ratios (45/120), our ballpark showed 35-50% token savings with a session prefix cache + moderate batching.
[02:12] Marta: 35-50% wow, that's material. what about throughput impact?
[02:16] Priya: batching increases throughput — if you can tolerate 10-30ms extra latency per request to wait for a batch window, you get much better tokens/sec. we recommend an adaptive batch window: tight for p95-critical, relaxed for background scoring.
[02:30] Ethan: our clients expect near real-time. 120ms p95 is strict — is batching compatible?
[02:35] Priya: yes, with continuous batching and small windows we hit micro-batching effectively; also prefix cache means per-request token generation is shorter so latency drops even with batching.
[02:46] Speaker 1: mhm, yeah.
[02:48] Jordan: let's switch to the console — i'll share my screen and run a quick cost sim. (screen) ok loading the Optimize tab.
[03:02] Jordan: here we can toggle batching concurrency targets, prefix cache hit rate, and KV lookup latency. i'm going to load a scenario named "aurum-score-45-120" we prepared.
[03:18] Jordan: baseline — no caching, minimal batching, hosted LLM variant — estimated cost is $0.0072 per scored request at your average tokens. p95 latency ~110ms in our sim.
[03:31] Marta: baseline cost is similar to our current invoice, yes.
[03:34] Jordan: flip on prefix cache with 70% hit rate — cost drops to $0.0046 per request, that's ~36% savings. p95 stays around 115ms.
[03:51] Ethan: is that assuming colocated cache?
[03:53] Priya: the sim assumes a 0.8ms local cache hit; for remote KV we show two numbers — with remote KV and 5ms lookup, savings still exist but p95 increases by ~8ms.
[04:06] Ravi: how do you measure hit rate in production? what's realistic?
[04:10] Priya: hit rate is empirical — we recommend starting with instrumentation via Redwood Console traces; look at session reuse stats. in many customer chat scenarios, 60-80% hit rates are common after a small TTL tuning.
[04:22] Marta: TTL meaning how long you keep prefix in memory?
[04:24] Priya: yes, and also how you segment keys — if you include user-level static metadata in prompt, it inflates prefix; better to store static bits separately in KV and only cache conversational tokens.
[04:36] Jordan: next, batching — i'm going to slide concurrency from 1 to 8 and show throughput/lambda.
[04:45] Jordan: with concurrency 4 and an adaptive 15ms batch window, tokens/sec climbs 2.7x and cost per request drops further to $0.0038. p95 latency moves to ~125ms in the sim for worst-case spike, but median stays <60ms.
[05:05] Ethan: median is fine, but p95 bump worries us for SLAs to partners. can we do hybrid?
[05:10] Priya: yes — route priority traffic to a low-latency lane: dedicated small fleet pinned to low-batch windows; lower-priority traffic uses aggressive batching. Redwood routing policy supports that out of the box.
[05:20] Marta: that's promising. what about dedicated vs hosted costs? we'd consider dedicated if predictable.
[05:24] Jordan: dedicated gives predictable throughput and you control quantization/variants. in our spreadsheet we show break-even for you at ~1.2M scored requests/month. below that hosted often wins for capex simplicity.
[05:37] Ravi: what's included in the dedicated SLA?
[05:39] Jordan: 99.9% uptime, burst capacity, and a patching schedule we coordinate. plus private deployment options with VPC peering for data residency.
[05:48] Speaker 2: okay.
[05:50] Priya: let's show a pathological case — long session history where users paste long docs. KV approach shines here: do partial retrievals for only the last N chunks and avoid resending the whole doc.
[06:02] Marta: can we evict parts of the prefix incrementally?
[06:04] Priya: yes, TTLs and LRU eviction policies; Optimize recommends TTLs by analysing session heatmaps — hot sections kept longer.
[06:13] Jordan: i'm switching to the cost-model CSV view, you'll see line items for token cost, model variant multiplier, batching factor, and cache hit adjustments.
[06:23] Jordan: one important note — our model counts both input and output tokens; so even big savings on inputs matter a lot.
[06:30] Ethan: do you factor in GPU utilization / reserved capacity cost for dedicated?
[06:33] Jordan: yes, the dedicated model includes reserved GPU amortization. the sheet shows break-even points for different committed months.
[06:40] Marta: curious about security — we require SOC 2 and customer-managed KMS for keys.
[06:45] Jordan: we have SOC 2, and Private deployments support KMS/HSM integrations; the console logs will show audit trails. we'll send the security pack you requested.
[06:55] Ravi: about data residency, we need EU-only for some customers. does Redwood allow region pinning for hosted?
[07:00] Priya: yes, region pinning and private option for strict residency.
[07:05] Jordan: switching back to sim — i'll show sensitivity: if cache hit drops to 40% the savings reduce to ~18%, but batching still gives gains. so caching and batching are complimentary.
[07:20] Marta: can Optimize recommend cache keys automatically?
[07:23] Priya: yes, we have heuristics: session id + recent-turns or conversation fingerprinting. we can also ingest your traces and suggest a key schema.
[07:34] Jordan: i'm uploading a small trace sample now and running a quick analyzer (demo).
[07:40] Speaker 3: (typing noises)
[07:45] Jordan: analyzer suggests 68% of prefixes repeat across sessions within 24h. proposed TTL 30m for conversational recency, with exceptions.
[07:55] Marta: 68% higher than i expected, nice.
[07:58] Ethan: about implementation — do we need to change prompts much?
[08:01] Priya: generally minimal. you need to decide what to include in the cached prefix vs dynamic context; it's mostly engineering around key composition and retrieval hooks. Redwood SDKs have built-in helpers.
[08:12] Jordan: i'll note two implementation patterns: in-process prefix cache for lowest latency, or external KV with local LRU cache for scale.
[08:22] Ravi: any gotchas with quantized models? we plan to use int8 variants to save cost.
[08:26] Priya: quantization interacts with kernel choices but not cache semantics — it can reduce per-token cost significantly; we model variants with multipliers in the sheet. test outputs for accuracy with your eval set.
[08:38] Marta: do you support running eval regression alerts? we need to ensure quality doesn't degrade after caching changes.
[08:43] Priya: yes, Optimize ties to evals — we can set guardrails and regression monitors on prompt sets.
[08:49] Jordan: time check — we've got ~30 minutes left; do you want us to run the 2-week POC plan now or hold planning offline?
[08:58] Ravi: let's plan offline. first deliverables: cost sheet and traces sim, then we'll kick off POC.
[09:05] Jordan: ack. one more demo snippet — show hybrid routing policy (hosted + dedicated fallback).
[09:12] Jordan: the console graph shows cost vs latency curves per route. you can pin high-priority traffic to low-latency nodes and route overflow to lower-cost variants.
[09:23] Ethan: would that be automatic under heavy load?
[09:26] Priya: yes, Redwood can auto-failover by policy — if dedicated capacity is saturated it falls back to hosted variant with a compatible model. logs surface the reasons.
[09:36] Marta: last question: how long does setup take for POC?
[09:39] Jordan: usually 3-7 days to onboard traces and run initial sims; POC itself 2 weeks to tune TTLs and hit rates.
[09:46] Ravi: acceptable.
[09:49] Speaker 1: okay good.
[09:51] Jordan: wrap up — i'll send the sheet, recording, and the security pack. Priya will run the throughput sim once we get traces. next meeting: POC kickoff week of March 15.
[10:05] Marta: thanks everyone, super helpful.
[10:09] Ethan: thanks, talk soon.
[10:12] Priya: thanks all.

Auto Action Items (end): Jordan to send cost model + recording; Priya to run sim; Marta to provide traces.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard tokens and speaker swaps near 02:46 and 09:49; filler words kept.
